- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 1-2 days), leading to overshoot; cap forecast at 10-15% above recent peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model lags in catching the reversal; adjust forecast upward 1-2 days ahead of sentiment change.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 2-5%.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to err on conservative side; increase forecast by 1-3% to account for hidden momentum.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in early days of 30-day window; apply bias correction for first 5-7 days (e.g., +2% if sentiment is positive).
